Emma (People Ops): Quick Q — new hire needs to add an adult dependent (brother) who receives SSI/has long-term disability. What docs do we accept and is this a QLE? Can coverage be backdated?
Liam G: He moved in with me 2026-02-10, he's 26, on SSI and has a representative payee. I can get the SSA award letter and a physician note. Is that enough?
Olivia - Benefits: Short answer: usually yes if he meets the "adult disabled dependent" criteria (social security disability or equivalent long-term impairment) AND is primarily financially dependent on the employee. Docs we typically request:
- SSA award letter or SSDI decision
- Physician statement (brief, confirms disability and functional limitation)
- Proof of financial dependency or shared residence (bank statement, utility, lease)
- Guardianship or power of attorney if applicable
Send via secure upload or DM — do not email PII.
Emma (People Ops): Is the move-in a QLE? He wasn't on any employer plan before (was on Medicaid).
Olivia - Benefits: Move-in can qualify as a QLE (change in household) or if there was loss of other coverage. You have 30 days from the event to submit QLE docs to enroll outside open enrollment. If you miss 30 days, enrollment may need to wait until next open enroll. We can consider retro coverage to the start of the month of the event (e.g., 2/1) if paperwork supports it, but payroll adjustments may apply.
BenefitsBot: Reminder — QLE documentation must be received within 30 days of the event to process midyear enrollment. Retro coverage requests require proof of date (lease, utility bill, or official move-in doc).
Liam G: Okay — I'll gather the SSA award letter and a physician letter. Do we need to redact SSI amounts or SSN? Also, concerned about sending medical info over email.
Olivia - Benefits: Please redact SSN and any extraneous financial figures. Use the HR secure portal: https://hr.redwood.com/upload or DM me and I'll send the one-time secure link. For the physician letter, a short statement like "patient is unable to perform substantial gainful activity due to chronic condition" plus date is sufficient — we don't need diagnostic details beyond that. We treat these as PHI and store in our encrypted HR system.
Raj (Payroll): FYI — if benefits team approves an effective date of 2/1, payroll will calculate retro premiums and either withhold as a lump sum on the next paycheck or spread across N pays (employee preference). We'll confirm amounts after benefits confirmation.
Emma (People Ops): I'll track the 30-day deadline and ping when docs are uploaded.
Liam G: Uploading to the portal now. @Olivia - please confirm when you have them.
Olivia - Benefits: Got it — I'll review tomorrow AM and let you know next steps. :thumbsup:
